newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end with steep losses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end with steep losses.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed with steep losses and in the lower portion of daily ranges.
Modest short-covering trimmed the decline in the final minutes of the session, but the fall was negative for the near-term outlook.

"We could have another down day Friday and it could get scary," said one S&P 500 trader on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. He noted, however, that quarterly expirations recently have had "a positive spin" and the market could recover early next week.
Traders pegged pressure to a steep decline in bond prices, which fell after stronger than expected U.S. retail sales data and remarks by Federal Reserve vice chairman Alice Rivlin.

Rivlin said the economy was "perking along" and that the Fed must keep a watch out for an acceleration in inflation. She later told reporters that the Fed was not sure if the economy was growing at a higher than sustainable rate.
"The world seems to be convinced that the Fed has to raise rates," said Kurt Schultz, stock index futures analyst for Refco Inc on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Schultz noted, however, that the Fed's Beige Book released Wednesday did not point to any fast-paced acceleration in the economy or inflation.
Futures had opened lower on followthrough pressure from declines Wednesday. The Fed talk and steep declines in the bond market further pressured the market.
In addition, the break below 108-23/32 and 108-15/32 in the March bond contract also weighed on index futures, although March bonds recovered above the latter level in after-hours dealings.

Premiums of lead contracts narrowed on the decline, and arbitrage sell programs were triggered in June S&P 500s when the premium dipped below 7.00 to 6.90 points, which fueled declines in cash stocks, particularly early in the session, traders said.
June became the lead month in S&P 500s today.
Nikkei 225 stock index futures were soft during the session in tandem with declines in the U.S. market and following a drop in the cash Nikkei index overnight.

At settlement, June S&P 500s were off 13.45 points at 797.95, Nasdaq 100s rose 1.35 to 851.00, Russell 2000s fell 2.25 points to 363.25, Value Line futures were down 8.40 points at 718.50, Nikkei 225 index futures fell 435.0 to 17630.0 and Midcap 400s eased 1.90 point to 266.50.
